sites.name: Malapert A
sites.note: Near the pole the Sun stays within a few degrees of the horizon, so the surrounding relief decides illumination. With a LOLA horizon mask the Sun and Earth are measured above the real terrain horizon; without one, above a flat horizon.

sites.name: Mons Mouton
sites.missions: Intuitive Machines IM-2 Athena (landed March 2025); CLPS CP-22 (planned).
sites.note: Near the pole the Sun stays within a few degrees of the horizon, so the surrounding relief decides illumination. With a LOLA horizon mask the Sun and Earth are measured above the real terrain horizon; without one, above a flat horizon.

sites.name: Schrödinger basin (centre)
sites.note: Basin centre, not a published landing ellipse. Earth is never in view: needs a relay satellite.

model_notes: Terrain horizon from LOLA LDEM_75S_120M for Malapert A, Mons Mouton (observer 2 m, 250 km); flat local horizon elsewhere.
Orbit plane drift: lunar J2 secular term only.
Descent: deorbit to 15 km perilune, braking burn with 6 % losses, 60 m/s terminal margin.
Energy: share of the solar disc above the terrain over the first 5 days on the surface.
Ground stations: NASA DSN Goldstone, Madrid, Canberra, Moon above a 10 deg mask (our assumption).
